title: Same Surname, Opposite Ends: Alex Baker's 169, Jon Baker's Spoon
title_candidates: Same Surname, Opposite Ends: Alex Baker's 169, Jon Baker's Spoon
One Baker Up, One Baker Down
A 10 at the 14th and Still Eight Clear
theme: One family at both ends of the sheet: the man with three Wooden Spoons banked the Trophy on the opening afternoon and never let it go, while the defending champion propped up the field by 23 — and all around them Catalonia produced both the lowest and the highest rounds in its TEG history in the space of four days.
opening_hook: Open at the 14th on the Stadium in R4 — the eventual champion signing for a 10 (b25), then an 8 at the 17th (b43), and still walking off eight points clear. The gap between the scorecard and the result IS the story, and it lands harder out of sequence than it would in a chronological build-up.

trophy_storyline.subject: Alex Baker leads from the 5th hole of R1 to the last and wins the Trophy on 169, by 8
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: A man with 3 prior Wooden Spoons — and the Spoon in 2 of the last 3 TEGs — banked a 12-point lead on the opening afternoon and was never headed, taking his second Trophy despite a scorecard littered with double figures.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: 46 points in R1, built on 17 points across holes 8-12 (b40) and 13 more over 14-16 (b47), and he was 12 clear before the field had settled. Turn: he then stopped playing well and it didn't matter — R2 brought an 11 at the 18th (b36) and an 8 at the 16th (b46) inside a 106 gross that stands as the worst round ever recorded on the Tour course (cr02), and Patterson outscored him in both R2 and R4; but 44 points in R3, including 21 over holes 11-16 (b04), pushed the lead back out to 12 (b17). Resolution: a closing 38, with a 10 at the 14th (b25) and an 8 at the 17th (b43), shaved the margin to 8 and no further — 169 points, wire to wire (b05, b01), with the R1 and R2 leaderboards (b37) never once showing another name on top.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams, the reigning Wooden Spoon holder, wins the Green Jacket at +66 by 14
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: The man who took the Spoon in TEG 17 turned a wretched opening round into three of the best gross rounds of the tournament and a third Jacket, finishing with a personal best at the Stadium.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: R1 was a bonfire — a 9 at the 7th (b24), an 8 at the 17th (b20), eight shots bled across holes 3-5, and thirteen consecutive holes without a birdie until one finally arrived at the 15th (b31); he sat third, 27 over. Turn: a poor R1 followed by a strong R2 (b42) — nine points over holes 3-5 (b38), thirteen over 13-16 with four straight pars (b19, b26) — drew him level with Jon Baker's lead (b34) and ended a 20-hole tenure in front (b48), before four pars from the 2nd to the 5th in R3 (b16, b21) took the Jacket lead outright at the 2nd (b28). Resolution: 13 over par in R3 and 12 in R4 — nine points across 8-10 (b06) and a birdie at the 5th (b10) — an 84 gross that was his new personal best at the Stadium, improved by 8, and the Jacket by 14 (b02, b05, b17).

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker, defending Trophy champion, collects the Wooden Spoon on 126 — 23 adrift of the next worst
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The TEG 17 champion, with 4 prior Trophies and 4 prior Jackets, finished last in the field in 3 of the 4 rounds and was beaten by the width of a small county.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: he actually led the Green Jacket from the 5th hole of R1 and held it for 20 holes (b48), and closed R2 with 16 points over the last five holes without dropping a gross shot (b09, b13) — 39 points, off the bottom, apparently fine. Turn: R3 on the Stadium undid all of it — a 9 at the 4th (b39), the bottom of the Spoon race reclaimed at the 2nd, and 28 points on a day when the man above him scored 16 more. Resolution: 29 in R4 sealed it; last in the field in three of the four rounds, 8 shots worse than his last visit to the Stadium, and a final total of 126 (b14) — the Spoon settled long before the 72nd hole (b05).

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin's 84: the lowest round ever played at PGA Catalunya - Stadium, and what it bought him
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A genuine all-time TEG record — 84 gross, beating the previous Stadium best of 89 across 27 prior visits — was posted by a man who had already been last in the Spoon race and who still lost the Jacket by 14.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 produced an 11 at the 15th (b35), his worst hole relative to par of the tournament, and it dumped him straight to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race (b66). Turn: on the Stadium in R3 he went round in 84 — a new course record (cr01) and his own personal best there by 7 shots, 8 better than his last visit. Resolution: R4 gave it all back at exactly the wrong end of the round, four holes from the 14th to the 17th without a net par and nine shots gone (b45, b49), leaving the holder of 9 prior Jackets 14 behind Williams and the record as the only thing he took home.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson: 22 shots underwater by the 10th hole of the tournament, runner-up by the end of it
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The nearest thing to a challenge to the champion came from a man whose tournament began with the single worst stretch of golf anybody played, and who then set new personal bests on both courses.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: an 8 at the 3rd (b23) opened a run of eight holes in which he bled 22 shots (b18) and seven without a net par (b29), and by the 4th he was last in the Spoon race (b33). Turn: the same round's back nine was 14 points better than the front (b22), with 13 points over holes 13-16 (b30); R2 repeated the pattern — an 8 at the 4th (b15) and 11 shots gone over 6-10 (b32), then 16 points across 11-15 (b11) for a new Tour-course personal best of 94. Resolution: R4 brought nine points over 4-6 (b07) and, after a triple at the 14th and a double at the 15th, a birdie at the 17th to stop the bleeding (b03) — plus a new Stadium personal best of 93 and second place, 8 short.

discovered_storylines.subject: The closing stretch as the tournament's crime scene: holes 14-18, four rounds, both courses
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Almost every decisive gain and every catastrophe in TEG 18 happened in the last five holes of a round, on both courses, which makes the run-in the connective tissue of the whole report.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 ended in wreckage — Mullin's 11 at the 15th (b35), Williams's 8 at the 17th (b20), Alex Baker's serene run broken by a double at the 17th (b50), while Williams's only birdie of the day came at the 15th (b31). Turn: R2 turned the same holes into a points farm — Jon Baker's 16 across 14-18 without dropping a gross shot (b09, b13), Williams's four straight pars from the 13th (b19, b26) — even as Alex Baker took an 8 at the 16th and an 11 at the 18th (b46, b36). Resolution: the Stadium finished the job in R4 — Alex Baker's 10 at the 14th and 8 at the 17th (b25, b43), Mullin's nine shots gone from the 14th (b45, b49), Patterson's triple-double-bogey-birdie limp home (b03) — a tournament decided, and disfigured, after the 13th.

vehicle_fit_response.note: The blow-up inventory is real (Alex Baker 4, Jon Baker 3) and it runs through the closing-holes motif storyline as texture, but catalogue has framed two of the last three reports; the two Bakers finishing first and last carries this one.

why_the_champion_won: He banked it on the opening afternoon — 46 points and 12 clear — then never finished a round worse than 3rd of 5, the steadiest man in the field, winning R1 and R3 outright; Patterson outscored him in R2 and R4 and it changed nothing, because even an ordinary round in place of his worst would still have left the runner-up short.
storyline_note: Trophy still leads and the champion is in frame throughout, but the frame gives the Spoon equal billing rather than third place: the winner and the last man are brothers, and Jon Baker being the defending champion makes the pairing the most interesting thing in the tournament.
